facts.title: potential incident - chemical exposure at P-4101

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was first aid or minor property damage. The potential outcome was rated 4 against the site's consequence scale, above the 1 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control FIRE_WATCH_PROVISION: the provision and briefing of a competent fire watch was not in place, and the ICAM investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Confirm at the next critical control verification that the provision and briefing of a competent fire watch on P-4101, M-4101 and P-4105 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining fire protection systems, specifically testing and inspecting fixed fire systems. P-4101 (hydrocarbon transfer pumps) is in service for hydrocarbon transfer, single mechanical seal with pressurised barrier-fluid support. The task proceeded during transfer operations while the provision and briefing of a competent fire watch was not in place. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 17 March 2020 a potential incident was recorded on P-4101, M-4101 and P-4105 at Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility during transfer operations; chemical energy held as hydrocarbon was not released.
